_doc: GX2 interior lighting (docs/lights.md, src/lights.cpp). Read once at start-up. fixtures: per light asset its colour temperature (kelvin, 2700-3200 K for lamps and candles; converted to linear RGB, then blended toward white by kelvinSaturation, since the eye adapts to warm light indoors), intensity (1 = a 60 W bulb at 1 m; inverse-square falloff) and radius (m); they override the asset's own light block. rooms: per room type the ceiling fixture (none below ceilingMinArea m2), the table light put on a table or chest top, and lowCeiling (the flush lamp under ceilings too low to hang a pendant). hallway: pendants every spacing m (between minSpacing and maxSpacing) along halls at least minLength long, set between the windows (never within windowClear m of a window's centre line), endInset m from the ends. sconces: rooms of at least minArea m2 (and every hall) get wall lights either side of their doorways, fromDoor m from the door edge, at most perRoom; electric sconces in buildings whose id starts with one of electricIds, candle sconces or wall oil lamps elsewhere. dayScale: lamps are dimmed to this fraction of their output in daylight (fires and electric bunker lamps are not). ceilingAlwaysArea: rooms this large always get a ceiling light; rooms longer than zoneOver m get one per zoneLength m zone (the zones the dressing groups furniture in).
